# Names {#top}

The parts of this section make names from the values that identify a row: names of variables, of constraints and
of other things that a solver names. A `VarTable` names each of its variables `<name>_<key0>_<key1>...`, from its
own name and the values of the variable's row. `indexedName` makes a name in the same way. `std::format` and an
output stream write a column or a `Ref` with the same text.

A value is written in a name by the first of these rules that applies to it. If a rule writes a value as another
value, such as a column's value or an entity's primary key, the other value is written by the same rules.

- A column is written as its value.
- A `char` is written as the character.
- An enum that has no `std::formatter` of its own is written as its underlying integer.
- A `Ref` is written as the entity that it refers to. An empty `Ref` is written as an empty text.
- A `std::tuple` is written as its elements, joined by `_`.
- A value whose type has a primary key, such as an entity, is written as its primary key. If the primary key is
  a `std::tuple`, its elements are joined by the text that `primaryKeySeparator()` returns, or by `_` if the type
  has no `primaryKeySeparator()`.
- An integer or a floating-point number, other than a `bool`, is written as `std::format` writes it for `{}`.
- A text is written as it is.
- Any other value, such as a `bool` or an enum that has its own `std::formatter`, is written by its
  `std::formatter`.

If no rule applies to a value, the value has no name. A `VarTable` over a set with such a value in a column does
not compile. A call of `indexedName` with such a value does not compile either, and neither does `std::format` of
such a column or `Ref`.

A format spec, such as `{:>4}`, applies to a column in one of two ways:

- For a column of integers, of `char`, of an enum or of text, `std::format` applies the spec to the column's
  value, as it does for the value itself.
- For any other column, and for a `Ref`, `std::format` writes the name first and applies the spec to that text.
  The spec must be one that `std::format` accepts for a text.

In use: [the guide](../guide/names-and-logging.md).

## `indexedName` {#indexedname}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::indexedName` - function"

    ```cpp
    template <typename... Keys>
      requires(internal::nameable<Keys> && ...)
    const char* indexedName(std::string_view family, const Keys&... keys)
    ```

    Returns the name `<family>_<key0>_<key1>...` of a row, with each of `keys` written as the Names section describes.

    A `VarTable` names its variables with the same text. Each of `keys` is a column, a row or another value.

    The name is written into a buffer that belongs to the calling thread. If a key's `std::formatter` throws an
    exception, the exception propagates.

    - **Takes:** Each type in `Keys` must have a name by the rules of the Names section.
    - **Returns:** A pointer to the name, which ends with a null character. The pointer is valid until the calling thread calls `indexedName` again, so it is meant for a function that copies the name, such as a solver's function that names a constraint.
    - **Throws:** `std::runtime_error` if the name is longer than 255 characters.
    - **Cost:** No memory is allocated, other than by a key's own `std::formatter`. Numbers and texts are written without a format string.

## `operator<<` {#operator-shift-left}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::operator<<` - function"

    ```cpp
    template <typename Traits, typename T>
      requires(internal::column<T> || internal::ref<T>) && internal::nameable<T>
    std::basic_ostream<char, Traits>& operator<<(std::basic_ostream<char, Traits>& out,
                                                 const T& value)
    ```

    Writes the name of `value` to `out`.

    The text is the one that `std::format` writes for `value` with the format string `{}`.

    - **Takes:** `T` must be a column or a `Ref`. `T` must have a name by the rules of the Names section.
    - **Returns:** A reference to `out`.

## `OnFormatOverflow` {#onformatoverflow}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::OnFormatOverflow` - enum"

    ```cpp
    enum class OnFormatOverflow
    ```

    The action that a `FormatBuffer` or a `NameBuilder` takes when a name does not fit in its buffer.

    - `kThrow`: If a name does not fit, `std::runtime_error` is thrown. If a `std::formatter` throws an exception while
      a name is written, the exception propagates.
    - `kLogAndClear`: No exception propagates, and the functions that write a name are `noexcept`. If a name does not
      fit, a warning is logged. `FormatBuffer::format` then returns an empty name, and `NameBuilder` cuts the name.
      If a `std::formatter` throws an exception, a warning is logged. `FormatBuffer::format` then returns an empty
      name, and `NameBuilder::append` ends the name after the separator.

## `FormatBuffer` {#formatbuffer}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::FormatBuffer` - class"

    ```cpp
    template <std::size_t N, OnFormatOverflow Policy = OnFormatOverflow::kThrow>
    class FormatBuffer
    ```

    A base class that provides a buffer of `N` characters, in which a class writes one short name at a time.

    A short name is, for example, the name of a constraint that a solver copies. A class derives from `FormatBuffer`
    and calls its protected static member function `format`. `format` has the parameters of `std::format`: a format
    string and its arguments. It writes the name into the buffer and returns a pointer to the name, which ends with a
    null character.

    The buffer belongs to the calling thread. Each thread has one buffer for each specialization
    `FormatBuffer<N, Policy>`, and every class that derives from that specialization uses it. Therefore a `const`
    member function can call `format`, and two threads never write into the same buffer.

    The pointer that `format` returns is valid until the calling thread calls `format` of the same specialization
    again. Pass the pointer to a function that copies the name.

    A name has at most `N - 1` characters. If a name is longer, `Policy` decides what happens, as `OnFormatOverflow`
    describes.

    - **Takes:** `N` must be at least 2.
    - **Throws:** `std::runtime_error` if `Policy` is `kThrow` and the name that `format` writes is longer than `N - 1` characters.

## `NameBuilder` {#namebuilder}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::NameBuilder` - class"

    ```cpp
    template <std::size_t N, OnFormatOverflow Policy = OnFormatOverflow::kThrow>
    class NameBuilder
    ```

    A buffer of `N` characters in which names that start with the same root are built one after another.

    Each name starts with the root. `append` adds a separator and a token to the name, once for each key. The next
    name starts again at `rootLength()`, and its tokens overwrite the tokens of the previous name.

    A builder constructed with a null root is disabled. A disabled builder writes nothing, and `name()` returns
    `nullptr`. `restart` enables the builder.

    - **Takes:** `N` must be at least 2.

### `kMaxLength` {#namebuilder-kmaxlength}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::NameBuilder::kMaxLength` - constant"

    ```cpp
    static constexpr std::size_t kMaxLength
    ```

    The length of the longest name that the builder holds: `N - 1` characters.

### `NameBuilder` {#namebuilder-constructor}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::NameBuilder::NameBuilder` - constructor"

    ```cpp
    explicit NameBuilder(const char* root) noexcept(Policy ==
                                                    OnFormatOverflow::kLogAndClear)
    ```

    Constructs a builder whose names start with `root`.

    If `Policy` is `kLogAndClear` and `root` is longer than `kMaxLength` characters, the root is cut to `kMaxLength`
    characters and a warning is logged.

    - **Takes:** `root` must be `nullptr` or point to a text that ends with a null character. If `root` is `nullptr`, the builder is disabled. If the text has no null character at its end, the behavior is undefined.
    - **Throws:** `std::runtime_error` if `Policy` is `kThrow` and `root` is longer than `kMaxLength` characters.

### `enabled` {#namebuilder-enabled}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::NameBuilder::enabled` - member function"

    ```cpp
    bool enabled() const noexcept
    ```

    Checks whether the builder writes names.

    - **Returns:** False if the builder was constructed with a null root and `restart` has not been called since; true otherwise.

### `restart` {#namebuilder-restart}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::NameBuilder::restart` - member function"

    ```cpp
    std::size_t restart(std::string_view root) noexcept(Policy ==
                                                        OnFormatOverflow::kLogAndClear)
    ```

    Makes `root` the root of the names that follow, and enables the builder.

    After the call, the name that the builder holds is `root` alone. If `Policy` is `kLogAndClear` and `root` is
    longer than `kMaxLength` characters, the root is cut to `kMaxLength` characters and a warning is logged.

    - **Returns:** The length of the root, at which `append` adds the first token of a name.
    - **Throws:** `std::runtime_error` if `Policy` is `kThrow` and `root` is longer than `kMaxLength` characters. The builder is then left as it was.

### `rootLength` {#namebuilder-rootlength}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::NameBuilder::rootLength` - member function"

    ```cpp
    std::size_t rootLength() const noexcept
    ```

    Returns the length of the root.

    The tokens of each name start at this length. The root of a builder constructed with a null root has length 0.

### `append` {#namebuilder-append}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::NameBuilder::append` - member function"

    ```cpp
    template <typename Token>
    std::size_t append(std::size_t length,
                       const Token& token,
                       std::string_view separator =
                           "_") noexcept(Policy == OnFormatOverflow::kLogAndClear)
    ```

    Writes `separator` and then `token` into the name, starting at position `length`.

    The name ends after the token. What the name held from position `length` on is overwritten. `token` is written
    as follows:

    - An integer or a floating-point number, other than a `bool`, is written as `std::to_chars` writes it. A `char`
      is an integer here, so it is written as its number.
    - A text, which is a value that converts to `std::string_view`, is copied.
    - Any other token is written by its `std::formatter`, as `std::format` writes it for `{}`.

    If the builder is disabled, `append` writes nothing and returns 0. If `Policy` is `kLogAndClear` and the name
    does not fit in `kMaxLength` characters, the name is cut and a warning is logged.

    - **Takes:** `length` must not be greater than the length of the name that the builder holds. If it is greater, the name can end before `length` or hold characters of an earlier name. If `separator` is left out, it is `_`.
    - **Returns:** The length of the name after the token. If the name was cut, `kMaxLength`.
    - **Throws:** `std::runtime_error` if `Policy` is `kThrow` and the name would be longer than `kMaxLength` characters.

### `name` {#namebuilder-name}

!!! abstract "`dreamor::NameBuilder::name` - member function"

    ```cpp
    const char* name() const noexcept
    ```

    Returns a pointer to the name that the builder holds.

    - **Returns:** A null pointer if the builder is disabled. Otherwise, a pointer to the name, which ends with a null character. The pointer is valid until the next call of `append` or `restart` on the builder, or until the builder is destroyed.
